title: Adaptive oncogenesis of β-catenin emerges from declining liver tissue integrity
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76373-y

Despite being a common driver of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), oncogenic β-catenin is ineffective at initiating liver cancer on its own. Here the authors show that β-catenin mutations as a single genetic event confer negative fitness in the healthy liver, while driving clonal expansion and tumorigenesis as liver tissue integrity declines with chronic liver disease or aging.

title: Stratospheric impacts on Eurasian soil moisture on subseasonal timescales
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 08 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75786-z

This study shows that sudden stratospheric warmings reshape Eurasian soil moisture by increasing wetness over Iberia while warming-induced drying affects soils from the Iranian Plateau to northern India, revealing a source of subseasonal hydroclimate predictability.

title: Allele-specific chromatin architecture shapes imprinted domains and coordinates a distal enhancer and antisense transcription at the mouse Mest-Copg2 domain
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 08 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76506-3

Here the authors show that parent-specific 3D genome architecture is a common feature of imprinted genes and identify a distal enhancer that works with antisense transcription to regulate neuron-specific imprinting.

title: Cavity-Enabled Supramolecular Regulation of Capacitive–Redox Bromine Electrochemistry in Zinc–Bromine Batteries
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 08 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76539-8

Aqueous zinc-bromine batteries face a trade-off between capacitive power and redox capacity. Here, authors design cavity enabled supramolecular that dynamically switch from ion storage at low voltages to polybromide stabilization at high voltages, delivering high capacity, power and cycling durability.

title: Human learning of probability distributions is biased toward moderate structural complexity
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 08 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76247-3

Humans build internal models from online observations to adapt to new environments. Here, the authors show that individuals are biased towards building models with moderate structural complexity, regardless of true complexity.

title: Targeting m<sup>6</sup>A writer METTL3 with engineered nanovesicles reduces neuroinflammation in vitro and in vivo
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 08 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75862-4

Strategies to modulate neuroinflammation have broad therapeutic potential. Here, the authors develop siMETTL3-hNVs, nanovesicles carrying siRNA targeting METTL3, and show they can reduce neuroinflammation in vitro and in vivo.

title: Diet-responsive proteogenomic effects following short-term restriction of animal products in humans
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 08 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76379-6

Using longitudinal proteogenomics, the authors reveal diet- and season-sensitive genetic effects on protein abundance linked to cholesterol and methionine metabolism and to immune function.

title: Self-Assembled Multilayers Reduce Interfacial Energy Loss in Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 08 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76497-1

Self-assembled interlayers improve perovskite solar cells but suffer aggregation, incomplete coverage, and weak interfaces, limiting efficiency and stability. Pan et al. design a methoxy-functionalized molecule improving wettability and interface contact, boosting efficiency and long-term stability.
